chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Sawadah al-Qattan and 'Ali ibn Asbat, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, who said:
We said to him: May we be your ransom, sacrificial animals have become scarce for us in Makkah; is it sufficient for two people to share in one sheep? He said: Yes, and on behalf of seventy.

The discussion concerning these reports, despite the variation in their wording and the incompatibility of their meanings, is from two angles. One of them is that there is nothing in any of them explicitly stating that sufficiency on behalf of seven, or five, or seventy—according to the variation of their wordings—applies to the obligatory offering or the supererogatory one; so when there is no explicit statement about that, we interpret them to mean that what is intended is that which is not obligatory, not that which is an obligatory duty. This is because in the obligatory case, only one on behalf of one is sufficient, according to what we mentioned first; and that which indicates this interpretation is...

key_terms.التَّطَوُّعِ: that which is voluntary or supererogatory
key_terms.الْأَضَاحِيُّ: sacrificial animals offered for ritual slaughter
key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: the sacrificial offering associated with hajj rites
key_terms.الْوَاجِبِ: that which is obligatory as a legal duty
key_terms.سَبْعِينَ: seventy, indicating the reported extent of shared sufficiency
key_terms.شَاةٍ: a sheep used as a sacrificial animal
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the location in which the scarcity is mentioned

ai.seo_question: Can multiple people share in one sacrificial animal for hajj, and does this apply to obligatory hady?
ai.summary: This report discusses whether multiple people may share in a single sacrificial animal during hajj when sacrificial animals are scarce in Makkah. The accompanying legal discussion clarifies that such reports are interpreted as referring to non-obligatory offerings, whereas an obligatory hady is only sufficient for one person on behalf of one person.
